questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Romania?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Romania article.

questions.proof: The capital and biggest city in Romania is Bucharest (Romanian: București ), with a population of 1.6 million.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Romania about 238,397 square kilometres; Syria about 185,180 square kilometres; Serbia about 88,499 square kilometres; Switzerland about 41,291 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Bucharest?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Romania is Bucharest.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Romania on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Romania on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Romania?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Romania on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Romania article.

questions.proof: Most of Romania's border with Serbia and Bulgaria is made by the Danube.
